en: The Poṣadhavastu. Summary Verse (Piṇḍoddāna): Poṣ-v 1. (53v = GBM 6.707) The summary verse is as follows: [text follows]
The heretics, Kapphiṇa, the dwelling place, the monks, and the final colloquy.
Poṣ-v 2. Summary verse (uddāna):
The heretics said, "Why is the Poṣadha not performed?
They do not sit together in common agreement; where could one recite the Poṣadha?"
Poṣ-v 3.1. The Blessed One was staying at Rājagṛha in the Bamboo Grove, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Poṣ-v 3.2. Now at that time, many lay followers from Rājagṛha were devotedly intent day after day on approaching the Blessed One for the purpose of seeing him and attending upon him.
Poṣ-v 3.3. Then this thought occurred to those many lay followers from Rājagṛha: "It is still too early for us to approach the Blessed One for the purpose of seeing him and attending upon him."
"The Blessed One is in seclusion, and the monks worthy of mental cultivation are also in seclusion; what if we were to go to the monastery of the wanderers of other sects?

(Poṣ-v 3.4). Then a great number of lay followers from Rājagṛha went to the monastery of the wanderers of other sects, and having arrived, they exchanged greetings with the wanderers of other sects face-to-face.
Having exchanged various pleasing conversations, they sat down in a secluded place.

(Poṣ-v 258) Poṣ-v 3.5. Then a certain non-Buddhist ascetic said this to the other non-Buddhist ascetics: "Friends, is the sitting, the ritual action, and the *poṣadha* ceremony known only to us, or is it also known to the śramaṇas?"
[This] is also [the case] for the followers of the Śākya-son (Śākyaputrīya).

Poṣ-v 3.6. Then a certain heretic said this to the heretics: "Sirs, sitting, ritual action, and the *poṣadha* are known only among us, but not at all among the śramaṇas who are followers of the Śākya-son.
Poṣ-v 3.7. Then many lay followers (*upāsaka*) from Rājagṛha [approached] many wandering mendicants of other sects...
They neither rejoiced in what was spoken nor did they reject it; without rejoicing or rejecting, they rose from their seats and departed.
They approached the Blessed One, and having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, the lay followers of Rājagṛha related to the Blessed One the entire conversation that had occurred between them and the many other wandering ascetics of other sects.
They reported this in detail and spoke thus: "O, would that the Blessed One, out of compassion, would also prescribe for us the sitting together, the ritual action, and the *poṣadha*.
The Blessed One consented to the many lay followers of Rājagṛha by remaining silent.

(POṢ-V 260) POṢ-V 3.11. Then many lay followers from Rājagṛha, understanding through the Blessed One’s silence that he had consented, rejoiced and delighted in what the Blessed One had spoken, and departed from the presence of the Blessed One.
Poṣ-v 4. Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the monks:
"Therefore, I authorize that from this day forward, the monks shall perform the formal sitting (*niṣadyā*) and observe the *poṣadha*.
Poṣ-v 5.1. It was said by the Blessed One: "From this day forward, the monks shall perform the formal sitting and observe the *poṣadha*."
They did not know what the sitting was, what the ritual action was, or what the *poṣadha* was.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"Sitting" refers to yoga. Come, monks, contemplate this very body— up from the soles of the feet and down from the hair of the head, bounded by the skin— exactly as it is, exactly as it has come to be, full of various kinds of impurities.
In this body there are: head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, dust, filth, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys,
heart, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach, large intestine, abdominal fat,
liver, excrement, tears, sweat, saliva, nasal mucus, grease, lymph, marrow, fat, bile, phlegm, and pus.
Blood, the skull,
the brain matter, and urine.
(Poṣ-v 262)

The Blessed One said, "Yoga must be practiced. Thus, even when the monks had gone out for alms, they continued to practice yoga. They encountered a wandering elephant, and they encountered a wandering horse and a wandering foot-soldier; they fell down, and those who lacked faith mocked them.
"Noble ones, do you not see?
They replied,
"We are practicing meditation."
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"One who has gone out for alms should not practice yoga."
They practiced yoga in the gateway chamber and shook it about;
those lacking faith mocked them.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Yoga should not be practiced in the gateway chamber."
(Poṣ-v 264) Poṣ-v 6.3. They cause them to be carried up to the palace;
that very same disadvantage occurs.
The Blessed One said:
"A monk must not practice yoga in a palace. Yet they practiced it in their lodgings.
Those who practice meditation do not attain one-pointedness of mind because of the noise of thorns.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One,
and the Blessed One said:
One should not practice yoga in a dwelling.
They cultivate it in the forest;
thus they become accessible to thieves, rogues, lions, tigers, and leopards.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Yoga should not be cultivated in the forest."
Having gathered near a village, they meditated;
those lacking faith mocked them.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"That area should be enclosed with branches or with stakes."
It was covered [with a cloth]. The faithless ones mocked it, saying, "Noble ones, what is this enclosure? Is it for a cucumber or for a radish?"
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"That place should be surrounded by walls or moats."
It was covered [with cloth].
The faithless mocked them, saying, "Noble ones, what is this enclosure? Is it for citron, or for pomegranate?"
They said, "We are practicing yoga.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:

"Therefore, I authorize that a hall for exertion (prahāṇa-śālā) should be constructed. [Poṣ-v 7] It was said by the Blessed One, "A hall for exertion should be constructed," but they did not know what kind of hall for exertion it should be.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
There were two meditation halls,
a small one and a large one;
the small one had two cells.
In the middle was a large tunnel,
ten or twelve *layanas* long.
After the monks had constructed a *layana*, they did not leave the door open as it should have been secured.
The Blessed One said:
"The door must be opened.
The monks did not provide a bolt.
The Blessed One said:
"A door-bolt must be provided;
it is difficult to open."
The Blessed One said:
"A long cloth should be given.
He made a sound.
The Blessed One said:
"A piece of leather should be placed underneath;
it is bound with difficulty."
The Blessed One said:
"It becomes dark."
The Blessed One said:
"A window must be opened.
They opened it at the bottom.
They become accessible to thieves, rogues, lions, and tigers.
The Blessed One said:
"He must not be released from below."
They let it go from above;
that very same fault occurred.
The Blessed One said:
It must not be released from above;
two parts are to be discarded. Having discarded them, [it is to be placed] on the third.
When a portion was to be released,
they, having set aside two portions from above, released it from below.
The Blessed One said:
"Having discarded two parts from below, it should be released in the third part from above.
(Poṣ-v 9.5) The monks made [the robes] wide on the outside and narrow on the inside.
The Blessed One said:
The window should be shaped like the ocean:
closed on the outside and wide on the inside.
Crows, ravens, and pigeons enter it.
The Blessed One said:
"A latticed window must be made."
The Tryambukas and Trailāṭas enter.
The Blessed One said:
"A door-bolt must be provided."
Poṣ-v 9.8. It is opened by the wind.
The Blessed One said: "... [the doors] should be given.
Poṣ-v 9.9. It is fastened with difficulty.
The Blessed One said: "... it should be given.
"Suffering is being uncovered.
The Blessed One said:
Having made it into a staff with no footprints, it should be bound;
it should be opened by means of staffs with no footprints.
In that case, there is need for a seat. *Poṣ-v 10.1*.
The Blessed One said:
"Seats made of clay should be made.
They became hard.
The Blessed One said:
"A bench should be made.
It was stated by the Blessed One that a bench should be made.

They did not know what kind of pedestal it was. The Blessed One said: "It should be made such that... [The text here is fragmentary; based on the context of similar passages, a likely reconstruction is: "...it should be made with a base consisting of a lotus."
Thereafter, the arrows should be given by means of counting sticks (*vāna*).
(Poṣ-v 274) Poṣ-v 10.4. They do not know how many arrows there are.
The Blessed One said: "There are five kinds of arrows: those made of muñja grass, śāṇa grass, vālvaja grass, fine cloth, and cane."
They became hard.
The Blessed One said:
"Cotton mattresses should be spread."
The Blessed One said, "Cushions (tūlikā) should be spread out.
They did not know what kind of cushions they were.
The Blessed One said:
It should be four cubits in length and two across;
having made it of double thickness, it should be sewn,
and thereafter it should be stuffed with cotton wool.
They did not know how many kinds of mattresses there were.
The Blessed One said:
"There are five kinds of mattresses."
Cotton from the *arka*, *kāśika*, *eraka*, *āvaka*, and *śālmalī* trees; furthermore, there are five other types of cotton:
wool, hemp, flax, *nantaka* cloth, and dust-cotton.
They become filled;
all that cotton goes to one place.
The Blessed One said:
A "crow's foot" mark should be made with a thread between [the sections].
(Poṣ-v 276)
They sit down and sway about.
The Blessed One said:
"A ghaṭī [time-measuring device] should be maintained."
It falls off.
The Blessed One said:
"Having tied it with a thread and fastened it to the ear, it should be worn."
Even so, they continued to shake it. The Blessed One said: "The staff should be used."
The monks were performing the *kalamacchedya* (the cutting of the rice stalks).
It caused a wound. The Blessed One said:
"They should be cut off.
Even so, it continues to grow.
The Blessed One said:
"Having wrapped it with strips of cloth, it should be moved slowly.
Even so, they still shook it.
The Blessed One said:
The ball should be thrown.
(Poṣ-v 278) Poṣ-v 11.7. The monks threw it in the dark.
He does not see it.
The Blessed One said:
"It should be tied with strings and thrown [into the water], and then it should be drawn back again."
Thereafter, he should be drawn back again.
Nevertheless, they continue to shake him.
The Blessed One said:
"A lamp should be placed in front.
Nevertheless, they still moved it about. The Blessed One said:
"One foot should be set down.
Even so, they continued to move about.
The Blessed One said:
The second quarter [of the verse] should be introduced:
"Nevertheless, they cause it to waver.
The Blessed One said:
Having risen, one should practice walking meditation.
Monks... {Cf. SHT VIII (Erg. 1033v1: monks practice walking meditation... a waistband should be tied.}
The Blessed One said: ... [They] hold it with their hands.
The Blessed One said:
... while walking, they should not walk wearing sandals;
[if] they walk wearing sandals, they make noise.
The Blessed One said:
"One should not walk about while wearing sandals."
The two feet become covered with dust.
The Blessed One said:
"A black woolen rug (kālakutha) should be spread out."
It became oily. The Blessed One said:
"Monks, I shall prescribe the rules of customary conduct for a monk who is an ascetic."
A monk who is a forest-dweller (*prāhāṇika*) should wash his feet every third day.
If a forest-dwelling monk does not undertake and abide by the rules of customary conduct as they have been prescribed, [he commits an offense].
One incurs an offense of transgression.
They did not measure it there.
The Blessed One said:
"A second city should be built above.
"It is difficult to ascend," [they said].
The Blessed One said:
"Stairways should be constructed.
A precipice occurred;
the Blessed One said:
A railing should be constructed.
It shook. The Blessed One said:
"They should be pinned with iron spikes.
Even so, they did not measure it.
The Blessed One said:
Or else, a row of shelters should be constructed outside;
they also construct finished doors.
They looked at one another.
The Blessed One said: "The doors must be opened."
They moved about there.
The Blessed One said:
"Having hung a cloth or a strip of cloth at the base of the door, one may lie down; no remorse should be felt in this matter."
They have departed from there;
they do not return.
The Blessed One said:
A monk who is a supervisor of the relinquishment [of robes] should be appointed.
Poṣ-v 16.1. A monk endowed with five qualities who has not been appointed as a supervisor of the relinquishment of robes should not be appointed;
and one who has been appointed should be dismissed.
By which five?
He goes out of desire, he goes out of hatred, he goes out of delusion, he goes out of fear;
whether awake or asleep, he does not know the abandonment [of unwholesome states].

(Poṣ-v 284) A monk endowed with these five qualities who has been appointed as a supervisor of the relinquishment of offenses should not be appointed if he has not yet been appointed; and if he has been appointed, he should be dismissed.

Poṣ-v 16.2. A monk endowed with five qualities who is the overseer of the relinquishment [of robes] should be appointed if he has not yet been appointed; and once appointed, he should not be dismissed.
What are the five?
He does not act out of desire, nor out of hatred, nor out of delusion, nor out of fear;
he knows the abandonment [of faults] whether it has been undertaken or not undertaken.
A monk endowed with these five qualities who is the overseer of abandonment, if not yet appointed, should be appointed.
And once he has been approved, he must not be set aside. (Poṣ-v 17.1) Furthermore, he is to be approved in this manner:

(Poṣ-v 17.2) Having prepared the seating and bedding, having struck the ghaṇṭī, and having exhorted the monks by means of an inquiry, when the entire Saṃgha is seated and assembled, one monk should ask:
"Do you, [name], venture to take charge of the Sangha’s meditation retreat?
He should reply, "I venture."
Poṣ-v 17.3. Thereafter, one monk, having made a formal motion (jñapti), should perform the ritual act (karman).
Poṣ-v 17.4. "Let the venerable Saṃgha listen!
This monk named so-and-so, the overseer of the meditation retreat, is capable of overseeing the meditation retreat for the Saṃgha."
If it seems timely to the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha consent and authorize that the Saṃgha should appoint such-and-such a person as the overseer of the retreat;
the monk named so-and-so, as the overseer of the retreat, will attend to the Saṃgha’s retreat.
This is the motion (*jñapti*).
And the formal act (karman) should be performed in this way:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen.
The monk named so-and-so, the overseer of the retreat, is capable of overseeing the Saṃgha’s retreat."
b. Therefore, let the Saṃgha appoint a monk named so-and-so as the overseer of the retreat;
this monk named so-and-so, as the overseer of the retreat, shall attend to the Saṃgha’s retreat.
(Poṣ-v 288)

c. For those venerable ones who approve of appointing the monk named so-and-so as the overseer of the retreat—so that the monk named so-and-so shall oversee the retreat for the Saṅgha—let them remain silent;
those who do not approve should speak.
The monk named so-and-so has been approved by the Saṃgha as the overseer of the retreat.
This monk named so-and-so will oversee the retreat for the Saṃgha.
Since there is silence, it is thus agreed and permitted by the Saṃgha.
I shall maintain this.
Poṣ-v 18. I will prescribe the rules of customary conduct for a monk who is the attendant of the meditation hall (*prahāṇapratijāgraka*).
The monk who is the attendant of the meditation hall must sprinkle water upon the meditation hall.
It must be swept clean;
a gentle coating of cow dung should be applied;
and the privy and the urinal should be repaired, sprinkled with water, and swept clean.
A tender layer of cow dung should be provided,
and a leaf-mat should be laid down.
"Clay and water should be set aside.
[The Buddha] went to each of them one by one and summoned them.
The Blessed One said:
No one should be summoned individually;
the gaṇḍī should be struck.
Thus, he had the gaṇḍī struck in detail.
When they had arrived, fully armed,
[the others] asked, "Noble ones, have bandits fallen upon us?
They replied:
"Sirs, we are not thieves; we have fallen ill, but rather we are keeping watch over our meditation. They replied, "Noble ones, you are keeping watch for the sake of causing harm!"
"How can there be abandonment in this case?
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One,
and the Blessed One said:
The gaṇḍī should not be struck at length.
Thus, there are five types of gaṇḍīs here;
[this one] belongs to the entire Saṃgha.
The gong for work; the gong for the shoulder-load; the gong for the exertion of meditation.
And there is the *āpadgaṇḍī*.
In that regard, those pertaining to the entire Saṃgha are three slow beats; these are the three strikes.
The *karmagaṇḍī* is struck three times;
the *aṃsagaṇḍī* and *muṇḍikā* are struck twice;
the *prahāṇagaṇḍī* is the *khakkhara*.
The *āpadgaṇḍī* [is struck] until they are satisfied.
During the remaining time, they may do as they please.
The Blessed One said:
Having recognized the time, they should act as they please: those who receive alms from the Saṃgha, having bathed, will enter the Saṃgha;
those who are alms-collectors (piṇḍapātika), having washed their hands and feet, will enter the village for alms.
They did exactly so, acting according to their pleasure.
The Blessed One said:
"In this very way, one should not act according to one's own pleasure;
rather, the *tṛdaṇḍaka* should be recited."
(POṢ-V 294) POṢ-V 21.2.
They speak too much.
The Blessed One said:
One should not speak excessively;
they, however, spoke little.
The Blessed One said:
One should not speak too little;
rather, one should speak in a complete and rounded manner.
They do not point toward the south.
The Blessed One said:
"A gift should be indicated.
(Poṣ-v 296)
The Blessed One said, "The dedication of the gift (dakṣiṇā) should be proclaimed.
They did not know by whom it should be proclaimed.
The Blessed One said:
"The senior monk of the Saṃgha should give the formal assignment," [it was said].
They assigned a great gift.
The Blessed One said:
"A large sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should not be prescribed.
They prescribe one that is too small.
The Blessed One said:
The formal act of dedication (dakṣiṇā) should not be recited too briefly; rather, the formal act of dedication should be recited in its entirety.
Poṣ-v 23.1. The monk who oversees the retreat comes behind everyone.
He went at the very front.
The Blessed One said:
"The monk appointed to oversee the abandonment [of defilements] should walk at the very rear."
One must come at the very head of all.
If such a circumstance arises, one should hide the curtain in a secluded place and say:
"Venerable sir, I have hidden the curtain in that place."
Having opened [the door], you shall enter.

Poṣ-v 23.3. A monk who is a supervisor of the practice of abandonment (*prahāṇapratijāgraka*) who does not undertake and abide by the rules of customary conduct as they have been prescribed incurs an offense.
Poṣ-v 24. This is called "sitting" (*niṣadyā*).
(Poṣ-v 298) Poṣ-v 25. What is an act?
It is a formal motion (*jñapti*), a motion followed by one proclamation (*jñaptidvitīya*), or a motion followed by three proclamations (*jñapticaturtha*) performed by the Saṃgha.
This is called the ritual action (*kriyā*).
[Poṣ-v 26] What is the *poṣadha*?
"O monks, that recitation of the *Prātimokṣasūtra* which has been taught by me to you should henceforth be recited by you every half-month."
The Blessed One said, "The recitation of the Prātimokṣa-sūtra should be performed every half-month. They did not know by whom it should be recited.
The Blessed One said:
"The senior of the Saṃgha must recite the Prātimokṣa-sūtra every half-month.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One: "The senior of the Saṃgha must recite the Prātimokṣa-sūtra every half-month.
The monks went to his dwelling.
They did not measure it there.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One,
and the Blessed One said:
A dwelling should not be assigned [to them].
They assign it to a palace;
even there, they do not measure it out.
The Blessed One said:
"The assembly should appoint a *poṣadhāmukha* (the presiding officer for the *poṣadha*).
It was stated by the Blessed One: "The assembly should appoint a *poṣadhāmukha*."
They did not know where they should perform the formal authorization (*saṃmantraṇīya*).
The Blessed One said:

Whatever site is established in all its aspects—bounded internally and with a precinct extending one *vyāma* externally—and which is approved by the Saṃgha as the place for the Uposatha, that should be authorized by the Saṃgha. And it should be authorized in this manner: Having prepared the seating and struck the gong, and having questioned the monks through a formal inquiry, when the entire Saṃgha is seated and assembled, a single monk should make the motion (*jñapti*).
Having performed the ritual action, it should be done as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This site, which is completely finished in every respect, within the boundary and with its surrounding area outside the boundary, is approved by the Saṃgha as the place for the Poṣadha ceremony."

If it seems the right time to the Saṃgha, let the Saṃgha grant permission: that the Saṃgha should authorize this site—completely finished in every respect, within the boundary and with its surrounding precincts outside—as the place for the Poṣadha ceremony of the Saṃgha. This is the motion.
And the formal act (karman) should be performed in this manner:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen.
This matter has been finalized in every respect; within the boundary and including the vicinity outside the enclosure, it is approved by the Saṃgha as the site for the Poṣadha."

b. Therefore, the Saṃgha authorizes this site—completely defined in all its aspects, within the boundary and including the surrounding area of one fathom—as the place for the Poṣadha ceremony of the Saṃgha.

c. Those venerable ones who consent to authorize this site—completely defined in all its aspects, within the boundary and including the surrounding area of one fathom—as the place for the Poṣadha ceremony of the Saṃgha, let them remain silent.
"It is not permitted that [they] speak.

It has been approved by the Saṃgha that this site—completely finished in every respect, within the boundary and including the surrounding area of one fathom—is the place for the Poṣadha ceremony of the Saṃgha.
It is accepted and authorized by the Saṃgha; since there is silence, I shall hold it to be so."

Poṣ-v 31.1. Wherever the Saṃgha has designated the place for the Poṣadha ceremony, there the monks, having sat down, shall perform the Poṣadha; they shall perform the formal acts (*karmas*) consisting of a motion (*jñapti*), a motion followed by one proclamation (*jñaptidvitīya*), or a motion followed by three proclamations (*jñapticaturtha*).
Poṣ-v 31.2. If they perform them while being discordant, they become guilty of an offense (*sātisāra*).
Poṣ-v 32. Summary verse (uddāna):
The boundary was established by Kapphiṇa; the robe was approved there. In a residence where no boundary has been fixed, there is the bringing forth and the preparation;
the ritual act and the Prātimokṣa—these five are declared as the headings.
(Poṣ-v 304) Poṣ-v 33.1. The setting was Rājagṛha.
At that time, the Venerable Brāhmaṇa Kapphiṇa was staying at Rājagṛha in the Senikā Cave, living in accordance with the community’s agreement for a common residence and a single *poṣadha* ceremony.
Then, on the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, many monks sat together and assembled at the commencement of the *poṣadha*, for the most part waiting for the Venerable Brāhmaṇa Kapphiṇa.
Poṣ-v 33.4. Then this thought occurred to the venerable Brāhmaṇa Kapphiṇa: "Today is the fifteenth-day poṣadha of the Saṃgha; it is also the fifteenth-day poṣadha for me, the monk Kapphiṇa.
Should I go to the assembly for the Saṃgha's poṣadha, or should I not go to the assembly for the Saṃgha's poṣadha?"
Should I observe the *poṣadha* together with the Saṃgha, or should I not observe it?
Should I go to the Saṃgha for the affairs and business of the Saṃgha, or should I not go?
Should I participate in the affairs and business of the Saṃgha together with the Saṃgha, or should I not participate?
And it was said by the Blessed One:
"For one who is always pure, O Phalguna, there is always the *poṣadha*."
"For the one who performs pure deeds, being purified, his vow is fulfilled.
Thus [it is said]. "I am pure, endowed with supreme purity.
Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the mind of the venerable Brahmin Kapphiṇa, vanished from the Bamboo Grove and appeared in the Senikā Cave before the venerable Brahmin Kapphiṇa.
Standing before him, he spoke thus: "Kapphiṇa, did it not occur to you, while you were alone, in seclusion, and in retreat, this reflection in your mind:
'Today is the fifteenth-day *poṣadha* for the Saṅgha; it is also the fifteenth-day *poṣadha* for me, the monk Kapphiṇa'? [And so on, as before,] up until: "his vow was fulfilled."
"I am pure, endowed with supreme purity. "So it is, Venerable Sir.
"Kapphiṇa, if you do not go to the assembly for the *poṣadha* ceremony, who else will go?"
You shall not experience the *poṣadha* together with the Saṃgha; who else shall experience it?
You shall not go to the affairs and duties of the Saṃgha; who else shall go?
You shall not experience the affairs and duties of the Saṃgha together with the Saṃgha; who else shall experience them?
(Poṣ-v 308) Go, Kapphiṇa, to the assembly for the Poṣadha; do not fail to go. Experience the Poṣadha together with the Saṃgha; do not fail to experience it.

"Go, Kapphiṇa, to the Saṅgha's business and the duties of the Saṅgha; do not fail to go. Experience the business and duties of the Saṅgha together with the Saṅgha; do not fail to experience them. (Poṣ-v 34.5) Then the Blessed One, taking the venerable Brahmin Kapphiṇa with him, approached the place where the Poṣadha ceremony was being held.

a. Inasmuch as a great boundary has been established in this residence by the entire Saṃgha through the formal agreement of dwelling together for a single Poṣadha;

It is possible, Upāli.

in that context, this is the expansion.

the circular area has been authorized.

Since, in this residence, a great boundary has been established by the entire Saṃgha through the agreement of dwelling together in a single Poṣadha residence..."
The small boundary has been established;
the circular area has been authorized.
Now, the Saṃgha releases the great boundary.
He releases the small boundary and dissolves the circle.
For those venerable ones for whom it is agreeable to release the great boundary...
To release the minor boundary and to dissolve the circle, he remains silent;
it is not permitted for them to speak.
d. This is the first formal motion; the second formal motion; the third formal motion. e. The great boundary has been released by the Saṃgha;
the small boundary has been released.
The mandalaka has been dissolved;
it is approved and authorized by the Saṃgha, since there is silence. Thus do I understand this.
(Poṣ-v 336)
Poṣ-v 54. In that case, if they so desire, they should be expanded; if not, they should be contracted.

As before, up to: "or a stake has been driven in.

having propped up both boundaries with a piece of wood, a staff, a peg, or a clod of earth, and having made the formal motion (*jñapti*), should perform the ritual act (*karman*).
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen.

as previously described, up to and including a stake that has been driven in."
The fixed boundary markers for the great boundary have been proclaimed in the four directions,
as previously described, up to the marker of the precipice.
If it seems the right time to the Saṃgha, let the Saṃgha, if it so consents and permits, bind a smaller boundary within these limits and authorize a formal assembly circle (maṇḍalaka).

A. As far as the stable boundary markers have been proclaimed in the four directions by the resident and non-resident monks in this monastery for the small boundary."

the stable boundary markers for the four directions of the great boundary have been proclaimed,
as before, up to a marker consisting of a precipice.
b. Therefore, the Saṃgha binds a minor boundary (khuḍḍalikā sīmā) within these markers;
it appoints a precinct (maṇḍalaka). Within those markers, by means of the agreement for a common residence and a common observance of the Poṣadha, it binds a great boundary (mahatī sīmā).
Excluding the wilderness and the lodgings, as well as the village and its precincts:
for those venerable ones who approve, let it be agreed that a minor boundary be established within these limits.

Within the boundary of those [previously established] markers, by means of a formal agreement for a common residence and a common observance of the *poṣadha*, they have bound a great boundary, excluding the wilderness and the lodgings, as well as the village and its precincts; those who approve should remain silent.
Those who do not approve should speak.
e. The Saṃgha has bound a small boundary (*khuḍḍalikā sīmā*) within these meeting points;

a circular area (*maṇḍalaka*) has been authorized. Within those meeting points, a great boundary (*mahatī sīmā*) has been bound by means of the agreement for a single *poṣadha* residence and communal living, extending as far as the forest and as far as the lodgings, excluding the village and its precincts.
And it has been endured and authorized by the Saṃgha, since there is silence; thus do I understand this to be so.

(Poṣ-v 58) Thereafter, having gone out from the small boundary and having prepared the bedding and seats within the large boundary, the monks' formal authorization for non-separation from their robes should be granted.
As before, up to:

b. united by what is not Dharma; c. divided by Dharma;
d. united by Dharma.
In that regard, one legal *poṣadha* procedure is when they perform it lawfully and in full assembly.
The Venerable Upāli asked the Buddha, the Blessed One:
"Venerable Sir, how many recitations of the Prātimokṣa-sūtra are there? "There are five, Upāli."
a. Having made the formal motion (jñapti) and recited the introduction (nidāna), they cause the remainder to be heard by way of oral transmission;
the Prātimokṣa has been recited and the Poṣadha ceremony has been performed by the Saṃgha.
b. Having made the formal motion and recited the introduction, and having recited the four Pārājika rules, they cause the remainder to be heard by way of oral transmission.
The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha has performed the Poṣadha.

Having made the formal motion (jñapti), having recited the introductory narrative (nidāna), having recited the four Pārājika rules, and having recited the thirteen Saṃghāvaśeṣa rules, they cause the remainder to be heard by means of oral transmission.
The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha has performed the Poṣadha.

Having made the formal motion (jñapti) and recited the introduction, having recited the four Pārājika rules, having recited the thirteen Saṃghāvaśeṣa rules, and having recited the two Aniyata rules, they cause the remainder to be heard by means of oral transmission.
The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha has performed the Poṣadha.
Thus, in detail, the fifth [section] is precisely the recitation of the Prātimokṣa-sūtra.
Poṣ-v 61. Summary verse: The monastery, the rains retreat, the newcomer, and the traveler; perform the poṣadha; and the night passes away; by the arising of the thought, the poṣadha is performed.
Poṣ-v 62.1. It may happen that many monks reside in a certain monastery. They think to themselves:
"The Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk; the Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk."
On that very fifteenth day of the poṣadha, the Prātimokṣa was not recited for any of those monks.
The Blessed One said:

That monk must be sought out by those monks through the avoidance of [sharing] dwellings, the avoidance of bedding and seats, the avoidance of [shared] work, the avoidance of [shared] gains, and the avoidance of [shared] attendants; whichever monk the Prātimokṣa is recited for—
if he is found, that is well.
If it does not succeed, those monks should not wait for another *poṣadha* in that residence; if they do wait, they become guilty of an offense.
Poṣ-v 62.2. It may happen that in a certain residence there are many monks who wish to enter upon the prior rains retreat. They think to themselves:
"The Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk; the Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk."
On that very fifteenth day of the poṣadha, the Prātimokṣa was not recited for any of those monks.
The Blessed One said:

That monk must be sought out by those monks through the exclusion of [other] dwellings, the exclusion of bedding and seats, the exclusion of duties, the exclusion of gains, and the exclusion of attendants—specifically the monk for whose sake the Prātimokṣa is recited.
If such a person is found, that is well; if not, so be it.
If it is not possible, those monks should not enter upon the earlier rains retreat in that residence;
if they do enter, they become guilty of an offense.
Poṣ-v 62.3. It may happen that in a certain residence there are many monks who wish to enter upon the earlier rains retreat. They think to themselves:
"The Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk; the Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk."
On that very fifteenth day of the poṣadha, the Prātimokṣa was not recited for any of those monks.
The Blessed One said:

"Those monks must seek out another monk by relinquishing their dwelling place, relinquishing their bedding and seats, relinquishing their duties, relinquishing their gains, and relinquishing their attendants—[seeking] whichever monk..."
The Prātimokṣa is recited;
if it is successfully completed, that is well.
If it is not successfully completed, those bhikṣus must not spend the preceding rains-retreat in that residence.
They dwell [there] and become guilty of an offense.
(Poṣ-v 352) Poṣ-v 62.4: It may happen, for instance, that in a certain residence there are many monks who wish to enter the rains retreat during the later period.
It occurs to them, "The Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk; the Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk.
Yet, on that very Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the Prātimokṣa is not recited for any monk at all.
The Blessed One said:

"That monk must be sought out by those monks through the exclusion from [use of] dwellings, the exclusion from [use of] bedding and seats, the exclusion from [performance of] duties, the exclusion from [distribution of] gains, and the exclusion from [the service of] attendants— whichever monk the Prātimokṣa is being recited for."
If it is accomplished, that is well;
if it is not accomplished, those monks must not enter upon the later rains retreat in that residence. If they do enter, they become guilty of an offense.
Poṣ-v 62.5. It may happen that in a certain residence many monks have entered upon the later rains retreat. They think to themselves:
"The Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk; the Prātimokṣa is being recited for such-and-such a monk."
On that very fifteenth day of the poṣadha, the Prātimokṣa was not recited for any of those monks.
The Blessed One said:
"Those monks, having reflected upon it, should remain in that residence for two months; during those two months..."

After the lapse [of that time], the monk for whom the Prātimokṣa is being recited must be sought out by means of avoiding his dwelling place, avoiding his bedding and seating, avoiding his communal labor, avoiding his share of acquisitions, and avoiding his attendant. (Poṣ-v 354)
If it succeeds, that is well.
If it does not succeed, those monks must not wait for another *poṣadha* in this residence;
if they do wait, they commit an offense.

The venerable Upāli asked the Buddha, the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, when resident monks hear that visiting monks are arriving who are holders of the Sūtras, holders of the Vinaya, and holders of the Mātṛkās,
how should they conduct themselves toward them?"

Those monks, Upāli, should go out to meet the monks who are holders of the Sūtras, holders of the Vinaya, and holders of the Mātṛkās, for their sake, for a distance of two and a half yojanas with parasols,
banners, and flags, if it is possible; if it is not possible, they should go out to meet them for a distance of five krośas with parasols, banners, and flags.
If it is accomplished, that is well;
if it is not accomplished, one should go out to meet him for three *krośas*, half a *krośa*, or at the very least even to the terrace with parasols, banners, and flags.
If it is accomplished, that is well.
If not, the ceremonial bath (*snātra*) shall be performed; an offering of oil (*snehalābha*) must be made to the Saṃgha.

They must be granted exemption from [the assignment of] dwellings, exemption from [the assignment of] bedding and seats, exemption from [the performance of] formal acts (*karma*), exemption from [the distribution of] gains, and exemption from [the service of] attendants.
(Poṣ-v 356)
Poṣ-v 63.3. If someone there should say this:
"Venerable ones, since the going forth is common to all, why do these monks deserve [the status of] Arhats and we do not?", he should be told this:

(66v = GBM 6.723) It may happen that on the very fifteenth day of the poṣadha, visiting monks have sat down and assembled, whether four or more in number, and they hear there the signs, marks, and indications of resident monks; namely, the sound of a staff, the sound of footsteps, the sound of clearing the throat, the sound of a key, the sound of a bolt, and the modulation of the voices of the resident monks.
It occurs to them:
"There are monks who have not yet arrived;
may those monks who have not yet arrived perish."
For this very reason, let them be apart; let them be far away; let them be beyond.
Seeking schism and intent on causing division, they perform the *poṣadha* after making a formal motion;
they recite the exposition of the *Prātimokṣa-sūtra*.
As before, up until they search for them with a resolute intention.
Having sought them with a resolute intention, they obtain them;
sitting together with them and having performed the formal motion (*jñapti*), they perform the *poṣadha* ceremony and recite the exposition of the *Prātimokṣasūtra*.

The resident monks (*pūrvakā bhikṣavaḥ*) are not guilty of an offense. (Poṣ-v 488) Poṣ-v 96. When the newly arrived monks have sat down and assembled, if the resident monks arrive only in small numbers.
Thus they are equal;
[or] more numerous.
Poṣ-v 97. Intermediate summary verse:
Division, doubt, distraction, and conceptualization;
they do not obtain [the fruit], and yet they obtain it.

Poṣ-v 98.1 A monk should go on the fifteenth day of the poṣadha from a residence where monks are present to another residence where monks are present, provided that the monks there are pure and hold the same views.

Poṣ-v 98.2 A monk should not go on the fifteenth day of the poṣadha from a residence where monks are present to another residence where monks are present, if the monks there are quarrelsome, contentious, and disputatious.
Setting aside those who initiate disputes or those presiding over legal cases, or in times of distress, a monk must go there with the entire Saṃgha.

On that very Uposatha day of the fifteenth, he should go from a residence containing monks to another residence containing monks, or to a non-residence where monks are present who are pure and hold the same view.

(POṢ-V 490) POṢ-V 98.4. A monk must not go from a residence containing monks to another residence containing monks on the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, nor to a residence containing monks that is currently empty, if there are monks present who are quarrelsome and prone to strife.
Setting aside those who cause dissension, those who cause disputes, and those who initiate legal cases, or in times of calamity, a monk must go there with the entire Saṃgha.
On that very Uposatha day of the fifteenth, he should go from a residence containing monks to a residence without monks;

from a residence containing monks to a non-residence containing monks; from a residence containing monks to a residence that is neither a residence nor a non-residence containing monks—wherever monks are present.
Being pure and of uniform view,

a monk must not go from a residence containing monks to a residence on the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*— whether that [destination] be a non-residence, a residence containing monks, a non-residence containing monks, or a residence-and-non-residence containing monks— wherever there are monks.

They become makers of strife, makers of quarrels, makers of disputes, makers of contention, and creators of legal issues— unless, in times of emergency, the entire Saṃgha has authorized them to do so there.
(POṢ-V 492) POṢ-V 98.7. On the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, a monk must go from a residence where monks are present to a residence where no monks are present;

from a residence where monks are present to a non-residence where monks are present; or from a residence where monks are present to a non-residence where monks are present—whichever place he reaches, it shall be comfortable for him.
Either by means of the body or by means of the mind.

On the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, a monk must not go from a residence where monks are present to a residence where no monks are present, nor to a non-residence where monks are present, nor to a place that is neither a residence nor a non-residence where monks are present— unless there is an emergency or the entire *saṃgha* is going together.

On the fifteenth day of the Poṣadha, a monk must go from a residence where monks are present to a non-residence where no monks are present, or from a residence where monks are present to a place that is neither a residence nor a non-residence, provided that upon going there,
he finds comfort either in body or in mind.

(POṢ-V 494) POṢ-V 98.10. A monk must not go from a residence where there are monks to a residence where there are no monks, nor to a non-residence where there are no monks, nor to a place that is neither a residence nor a non-residence where there are no monks, on the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, except in cases of emergency.
Or by the entire Saṅgha.

On the fifteenth day of the *poṣadha*, a monk must go from a residence where monks are present to a residence where no monks are present, or from a residence where monks are present to a place that is neither a residence nor a non-residence, such that upon arriving there,
he experiences ease either physically or mentally.
